questions.q: According to Salesforce's own definition, what kind of language is Apex?
options: A loosely typed scripting language
A strongly typed, object-oriented programming language
A markup language for page layouts
A query language only, with no procedural logic
questions.explain: Salesforce defines Apex as a strongly typed, object-oriented programming language that runs on the Salesforce Platform server alongside calls to the API.

questions.q: What is an anonymous block in Apex?
options: A trigger that runs on every object
A class with no access modifier
Apex code that is compiled and executed but not stored as metadata
A method with no return type
questions.explain: An anonymous block is Apex code that doesn't get stored in the metadata, but that can still be compiled and executed -- exactly what the Execute Anonymous window runs.

questions.q: Which keyword is NOT allowed on a user-defined method written inside an anonymous block?
options: public
private
static
void
questions.explain: User-defined methods inside an anonymous block can't include the keyword static.

questions.q: Where would you find the output of a System.debug() call after running Execute Anonymous?
options: In the org's Setup Audit Trail
In the generated debug log, on a USER_DEBUG line
In a popup dialog in the browser
Nowhere -- System.debug output is discarded by Execute Anonymous
questions.explain: The debug log's content includes the output of any calls to the System.debug method, visible on USER_DEBUG lines in the Log Inspector.

questions.q: Which tool is built into Salesforce specifically for writing, running, and debugging Apex interactively?
options: The Object Manager
The Lightning App Builder
The Developer Console
The Report Builder
questions.explain: The Developer Console is Salesforce's browser-based IDE, and it's where the Execute Anonymous window and debug log viewer live.
